trust_decision.summary: The SOCKS reply builder decides which local address to report to the client. With extNat configured and no remote socket (an early error, or a failed connect), the port is copied from the stack variable `sin`, which was never initialised, and is sent in the SOCKS4/5 reply.

landing_point.why: The summary names SOCKS4 replies, and socks.c CLEANRET is the only code that builds a SOCKS4/5 reply. The engineer would land on the exact fix site.

fix_sites.entry_point: SOCKS listener (socks service / standalone socks binary built WITHMAIN), any SOCKS4 or SOCKS5 request that ends before or without a remote socket, with -Ne / extnat set

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route found. The only candidate is the unchecked getsockname on clisock at src/socks.c:283, which leaves sin uninitialised if the call fails. A solver could argue that failure cannot happen on a connected socket.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: CONNECT/BIND must still report the remsock address and port with the extNat address substituted, and UDP ASSOCIATE must still report the clisock address with intNat. A fix that zeroes the reply, or always reports clisock, breaks NAT reporting and BIND port discovery. The fix commit's own title is about the non-NAT case wrongly reporting the client-side address.

O6_input_shapes: requests failing before a remote socket exists (bad command, auth failure, filter reject)
CONNECT whose connect fails and resets remsock to INVALID_SOCKET (src/common.c:774-776)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The second BIND reply (incoming-connection notice) built from param->sinsr after accept. One could add a path that sends it with sinsr not yet set.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It repeats the same v4/v5 reply-encoding code as the CLEANRET reply, and a maintainer could reorder the accept error handling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The SOCKS5 UDP reply header copies SAADDRLEN(&param->sinsl) bytes from `from`. If the families differ, bytes of `from` that were never initialised would be sent.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The length is taken from a different sockaddr than the one copied, a plausible size-arithmetic slip next to the same reply format.

O9_family: uninitialized memory disclosure (CWE-908) in a network reply

O10_build.project_tests: tests/run.py + tests/harness.py (Python, local); tests/cases/socks.py covers SOCKS4/5 CONNECT but not extnat/-Ne

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: memset(&sin,0,sizeof(sin)) at declaration: removes the leak but keeps the else branch overwriting the remsock address with the client-side address when extNat is unset

out_of_scope_notes: src/udpsockmap.c:407 copies the address length of sinsl from `from`; it may matter only with mixed address families, and I did not pursue it.
unverified: Repo size not measured; 3proxy is likely under 5 MB of source (possible tiny_repo).
Whether getsockname on clisock at src/socks.c:283 can fail in practice was not checked.
The advisory text itself was not available; the mechanism was inferred from the fix diff and the code.
